articleTitle: Micro-Doppler Separation in ISAR Imaging based on Complex Local Characteristic-Scale Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: In an inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) system, the micro-Doppler (m-D) interference caused by the fast rotation or vibration of the target's components would degrade the legibility of the image reconstruction. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel algorithm that is based on complex local characteristic-scale decomposition (CLCD). The Doppler frequency characteristics of the main body and the fast-rotating parts were analyzed in our study. Subsequently, the radar echoes were decomposed into a set of stable mono-components using the CLCD algorithm. Through the imaging process, improved geometrical features of the main body were obtained. The effectiveness of the proposed method was demonstrated through comprehensive experiments.

articleTitle: CIFT: Multi-Modal Image Matching Based on Construction-Invariant Feature Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: With the continuous development of remote sensing technology, the variety of new remote sensing sensors is increasing day by day. At the same time, the single-mode remote sensing image is increasingly difficult to meet the requirements of geological analysis due to its single imaging band. Therefore, the comprehensive application of multi-source remote sensing image has become a research hotspot in the field of remote sensing. Image registration is the prerequisite for the comprehensive application of multi-mode remote sensing image, and the accuracy of image registration directly affects the accuracy of subsequent data analysis results. However, due to the different imaging bands and imaging mechanisms of different sensors, there are large radiation differences between the registration image pairs, and they are affected by noise. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a multimodal image registration method based on the Construction-invariant Feature Transform (CIFT). To reduce the effect of noise on the phase consistency model, anisotropic filtering is applied to the registration image pairs, which can smooth the noise while preserving the structural information of the image. Then, the structural information of the image is extracted using phase consistency, and the high repetition rate feature points are extracted from the phase consistency map. Based on the phase consistency map, the maximum gradient index map (MGIM) is constructed for feature description, which has good robustness against radiation distortion. In the experimental stage, six different remote sensing images including optical, SAR, depth, lidar, infrared and day and night were used to test CIFT and three comparison algorithms (OS-SIFT, SAR-SIFT and PSO-SIFT). Experimental results show that the CIFT method is the only method that can successfully register 6 types of multimodal images, and the registration accuracy is within 3 pixels, and the registration effect is good.

articleTitle: Spectral-Spatial Attention Fusion Network for Semantic Segmentation of Optical and SAR Image
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Semantic segmentation of remote sensing images is a fundamental task in earth observation, and the fusion of multimodal information has been proven to be beneficial for improving segmentation accuracy. However, optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images, as the two most widely used remote sensing data, have great semantic differences due to their individual imaging mechanisms. How to effectively utilize optical and SAR images for joint semantic segmentation is a challenging issue. Therefore, we have proposed a novel spectral-spatial attention fusion network (SSAFNet) for multimodal semantic segmentation, which consists of three main components: the two-stream encoder-decoder network, spectral-spatial attention fusion module (SSAFM), and semantic segmentation head. Firstly, optical and SAR images were input into two independent encoder-decoder streams in parallel to obtain high-level semantic features of different modalities. Then, the features were fed into the SSAFM for deep fusion and thus into the segmentation head to obtain joint optical and SAR image segmentation results. Finally, we conducted comparative experiments on an optical-SAR paired dataset, demonstrating that the joint application of optical and SAR images can improve the accuracy of single-mode semantic segmentation, and the proposed network proved to be progressive by comparison with other methods.

articleTitle: Adaptive Multi-Scale Optical-to-SAR Image Matching
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Image matching is the critical technique for heterogeneous information fusion in the big data era. To solve the nonlinear radiation distortion problem between optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images, an adaptive multi-scale matching method (AMM) was proposed. First, the edge features of two images were extracted in combination according to their imaging mechanisms. Second, core point matching combining phase features was applied to adaptively determine the approximate offset between two image centers. Third, matching points were obtained by wavelet multi-scale matching. Finally, the geometric relationship of matched images was determined after the outlier removal using the fast sample consensus (FSC) method. The matching performance of the proposed method was quantitatively compared with that of histogram of orientated phase congruency (HOPC) and mutual information (MI). The experiment shows that the proposed method is superior to HOPC and MI in terms of matching accuracy and matching efficiency.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Wet Tropospheric Delay for HY-2C Altimeter Based on GNSS and ERA5 Data
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: HY-2C satellite equipped with a three-channel Calibrated Microwave Radiometer (CWR) for Wet Tropospheric Delay (WTD) correction for satellite altimetry was launched by China on 21 September 2020. WTD is one of the range errors in satellite measurements of Sea Surface Height (SSH), so verifying the accuracy of CMR WTD inversion is important to obtain high precision SSH. However, there are few researches on the evaluation of BY -2C CWR WTD at present. The objective of this study is to evaluate the accuracy of HY-2C CMR WTD using Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) and ECMWF Reanalysis vS (ERAS) data. The results of the evaluation in the coastal ocean show that there are some anomalies in CMR WTD and anomaly rate is about 3% for distances to the coast from 40 to 200 km. The results of the evaluation in the open ocean show that there are some anomalies with spare spatial distribution and anomaly rate is about 1% over the open ocean beyond 40km offshore. The accuracy of HY-2C CMR WTD are evaluated in this study, and the abnormal data in BY -2C CMR WTD products over the ocean especially in coastal ocean that need to be improved.

articleTitle: Rao Distance Based Spatial-Spectral Joint Feature Extraction and Semi-Supervised Classification for Hyperspectral Image
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: This paper presents a novel feature extraction approach for hyperspectral images, termed Spatial-Spectral Joint Principal Component Analysis (PCA) coupled with Rao distance-based t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (SSPCA-Rao-tSNE). Specifically, we apply the classical PCA method for spectral feature extraction while concurrently developing a Rao-distance-based tSNE algorithm to enhance the extraction of spatial features, particularly those with non-Euclidean structural characteristics. These spatial and spectral features are then combined through feature stacking to create spatial-spectral joint features. Furthermore, these spatial-spectral joint features are utilized in a semi-supervised graph convolutional network for hyperspectral image classification. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance achieved by our newly proposed SSPCA-Rao-tSNE approach and the corresponding semi-supervised classification method in comparison to several classical methods.

articleTitle: Interface verification and satellite-ground testing of high-precision time comparison system between LEO satellites and Beidou satellites
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: In recent years, LEO satellite systems have become a research hotspot for scholars both domestically and internationally, and their applications in military and mobile communication have rapidly developed. The Chinese space station also belongs to the LEO satellite system and has been fully built and entering the stage of application and development. The Chinese space station is equipped with a high-precision time and frequency system that includes hydrogen atomic clocks, microwave clocks, and optical clocks. The system outputs 100MHz and 1pps signals as inputs, and an inter-satellite test payload is configured on the Chinese space station to perform two-way time comparison and synchronization with the Beidou satellite, thus achieving high-precision time comparison between LEO spacecraft and medium to high orbit satellites. In this article, firstly, a ground testing environment is established to verify the interface of the high-precision time comparison system between LEO spacecraft and medium to high orbit satellites. The test results show that the information interface of the comparison system remains consistent. Then, a satellite to ground test system is constructed to achieve high-precision time comparison between LEO spacecraft and medium to high orbit satellites. Analysis of ranging data shows that the comparison accuracy is better than 0.3ns.

articleTitle: LiDAR-Based Point Cloud Data Processing Application Research
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: LiDAR technology is widely used for point cloud data acquisition in geographic mapping, ecological surveying, etc., which facilitates the research. The PointNet model is a pioneering representative of deep learning technology and semantic segmentation of 3D point cloud, which improves the network generalization ability through a large number of trainings, but at the same time there are problems such as loss of detail data, complex scene recognition accuracy lower, and incomplete local feature extraction. Attention mechanism is a technique in deep learning that enables the network to focus on valid data and discard invalid data in the process of image processing. The attention mechanism can make the local features of point cloud data under deep learning more distinctive, so that the local features can be extracted more completely and accurately. In this paper, we propose to use PointN et network, combined with our own collected dataset for semantic segmentation experiments. And the attention mechanism is introduced to improve the recognition ability of Point Net network as well as the accuracy of segmentation.

articleTitle: Geometric Correction Method Based on Aircraft Control Points for Space-Based Optical Satellite
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Geometric correction is one of the key steps in achieving accurate positioning of the space-based optical satellite, and the acquisition and accuracy of control points directly determine the effectiveness of the geometric correction. The traditional remote sensing geometric correction models are mostly based on ground control points (GCPs). However, GCPs are difficult to extract in some observed backgrounds with single features such as oceans, deserts and forests. On the other hand, when there are significant changes in the terrain (such as geological disasters, increase or decrease in vegetation, alternation of dry and wet periods, etc.), the probability of mismatched GCPs will increase significantly, affecting the accuracy of the geometric correction. In addition, the successful acquisition of GCPs places very high demands on the accuracy, coverage, and update frequency of the ground model, such as Digital Elevation Model (DEM). Considering the limitations of GCPs, this paper proposed an alternative aircraft control points (ACPs) in special areas where GCPs are unavailable. Compared to GCPs, the actual latitude, longitude and altitude of aircraft can be obtained through the Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) system, which has the advantages of high accuracy, real-time, and wide coverage. Furthermore, in scenarios with single feature where GCPs are difficult to obtain, the detection of ACPs is even easier. This paper also proposed a spatio-temporal based matching algorithm for detected tracks and ADS-B data, which constructs a weighted feature descriptor for distance, velocity and heading. Simulation experiments are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the matching algorithm and the feasibility of using aircraft as control points.

articleTitle: Remote Encrypted Transmission Method of Electronic Chart Based on RSA Asymmetric Encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: With the adjustment of the strategy of the Chinese Navy and the expansion of the navigation scope of the ships, as an important carrier of Marine environmental information display, the security and reliability of electronic chart data transmission have been gradually raised and significantly concerned. In view of the particularity of electronic chart data, this paper designs the remote transmission technology of electronic chart based on C/S mode, and puts forward the optimization scheme of remote transmission system structure based on TCP protocol. On this basis, through the technical analysis of the cryptographic system, the RSA asymmetric encryption algorithm is applied to the electronic chart remote transmission process, and the improved RSA algorithm for electronic chart encryption and decryption is constructed. Finally, the functions of generating public-private key pair, loading public-private key pair, public key encryption and private key decryption for electronic chart are realized.

articleTitle: An Improved Motion Compensation Approach for Low-Altitude Squint SAR
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: In the case of high squint synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging of low-altitude platforms, the motion error is range dependent. The traditional motion compensation (MOCO) method cannot improve the focusing effect at the near or far range. Additionally, in this situation, the squint angle variability is more pronounced and cannot be ignored, as it affects the accuracy of MOCO. To solve the problem, this paper proposes an accurate MOCO algorithm for low-altitude high squint SAR imaging. Considering the problem of squint angle changing with range, it corrects the traditional squint SAR imaging geometrical model, and utilizes an improved CS function to compensate for the range-variant motion error. Finally, the effectiveness and validity of the algorithm are verified through simulation and real data processing.

articleTitle: An Optimized 3D Tile Scheduling Method Adapted to Terminal's GPU DRAM
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: 3D rendering and visualization have become integral components of numerous applications. However, rendering large-scale oblique photogrammetry models on terminals with varying GPU capabilities poses significant challenges. One of the primary issues is the efficient allocation of GPU DRAM to handle the rendering workload. Traditional methods often struggle to balance memory consumption, leading to performance bottlenecks and inefficient resource utilization. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to handle this challenge. Our method focuses on optimized 3D tile scheduling, specifically designed to adapt the GPU DRAM capacities of individual terminals. By canceling tile requests that exceed the maximum rendering memory allocation, we prevent unnecessary accumulation of the tiles within the cache, thereby maintains the valuable memory resources. The experimental results show that the proposed method performs well in saving memory consumption and visualizing large-scale photogrammetry 3D models across different terminal capabilities.

articleTitle: Application of the Vision Transformer and Mask R-CNN Joint Algorithm to Assist Forest Decisions
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: With the continuous iterative development of remote sensing technology and deep learning algorithms, it provides strong support for the rational development, management, and protection of forest resources. This article proposes a Vision Transformer and Mask R-CNN joint algorithm architecture that applies NEON high-resolution remote sensing image data to achieve forest type classification and recognition, as well as single tree crown area instance segmentation. Research has found that the ViT algorithm performs well in large-scale data, but it relies on reasonable parameter settings, and the ViT model pre-trained through a large dataset outperforms the vast majority of other models at present. Mask R-CNN relies on the accuracy of data annotation, and models trained with a small amount of data can also achieve good training results.

articleTitle: Marine Target Direction-of-Arrival Estimation for Shipborne HFSWR Based on Stacking Meta-Learning Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: To improve the precision of target direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation in shipborne high-frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR), a Meta-learning strategy based DOA estimation method is investigated. The base learners included decision tree (DT) regression, ridge regression, support vector regression (SVR), and linear regression (LR) served as the DOA estimator in the Meta-learner model. The proposed model utilizes the output results of each base learner as input features for constructing a new training set, and then used to train an LR algorithm and obtain DOA estimation results. Simulation targets are added to the measured shipborne HFSWR data in order to generate samples for model implementation. The results show that the proposed method has better estimation performance than single base learner, classical MUSIC and DBF methods, and provides a new idea for shipborne HFSWR target DOA estimation.

articleTitle: High-Precision Geometric Positioning of Optical Satellite Images Assisted by LiDAR Data
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: To achieve automated optical high-precision geometric positioning of satellite images, this study proposes a LiDAR point cloud-assisted method for high-precision automatic positioning of satellite stereo images, taking advantage of the complementary characteristics of LiDAR data and optical satellite images in terms of geometric positioning. Firstly, we match the LiDAR depth image and the optical satellite image with the AWOG methods and take the corresponding points as virtual control points. Then, the Rational Function Model (RFM)-based regional network adjustment is employed to calculate the Rational Polynomial Coefficients (RPC) correction parameters. By utilizing the optimized positioning parameters of the satellite imagery, the geometric orientation accuracy of the satellite stereo imagery is improved. Experimental results based on LiDAR data and GF7 satellite stereo imagery demonstrate that the positioning error is controlled within 3 meters, meeting the requirements of 1:50000 mapping accuracy. This indicates that the method proposed in this paper can achieve high-precision geometric positioning to assist optical satellite stereo imagery using LiDAR data.

articleTitle: Rotated Object Detection of Ship in UAV Aerial Images Based on Improved YOLOv7
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Aiming at the difficulty of ship detection in UA V aerial images and the problem of ignoring its direction, a rotated object detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv7 is proposed. By adding the angle prediction dimension and introducing the Gray Coded Label representation method to discretize the angle, the accuracy of the angle prediction is improved. The backbone network is replaced by Swin Transformer, and its attention mechanism is used to improve the feature extraction ability of the model. Then the K-means++ algorithm is used to cluster the anchor boxes, so that they are more suitable for the overall distribution to improve the detection performance of the model. The experimental results show that the improved rotated object detection method improves the detection accuracy by 9.12 percentage points compared with the original YOLOv7 model, and it can provide effective technical support for the task of ship detection.

articleTitle: Research on Second and Eighth Order Digital Correlation Techniques for Distributed Synthetic Aperture Radiometers
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: To satisfy the requirements of high spatial resolution and high sensitivity for distributed synthetic aperture radiometers, and to reduce inter-satellite data transmission pressure, this paper presents a research study on high-speed signal processing based on a distributed system, discussing a mixed quantization asymmetric digital correlation method. On the basis of pure digital quantization correlation, a method of pairwise correlation between second-order and eighth-order quantization is proposed, and its correction formula from the digital correlation coefficient to the analog correlation coefficient is derived. Simulations of the influence of the correlation coefficient, quantization threshold, and sampling frequency on various digital quantizations were carried out using MATLAB software. The output of the digital correlator and the efficiency factor were derived, demonstrating that the proposed mixed quantization asymmetric correlation method can enhance the sensitivity of the synthetic aperture microwave radiometer system. The efficiency factor obtained from the second and eighth order correlation method proposed in this paper has increased from 63% for the traditional second order quantization to 78%, nearing the efficiency factor of the third order quantization correlation.

articleTitle: A Motion Target SAR Imaging Algorithm Based on Back-Projection and Scene Segmentation: Enhancing SAR Imaging of Moving Targets through Advanced Back-Projection and Scene Segmentation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: This paper presents an imaging algorithm for moving targets in airborne video synthetic aperture radar (SAR). The purpose is to address the problem of imaging multiple moving targets with different parameters in video SAR. The proposed method segments the imaging scene into multiple sub-scenes, and performs separate imaging for each sub-scene based on different velocity parameters. Under high-frame-rate video SAR conditions, the efficiency of the algorithm can be improved by imaging only the regions of interest, taking advantage of the characteristics of back-projection(BP). This method provides an imaging algorithm for targets with different velocity parameters at the same distance, and can adapt to imaging requirements under large squint angles. Finally, this paper uses a GPU-based parallel computing framework to further improve the efficiency of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Panoramic Image Position Optimization Based on Point Cloud
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: The problem of 3D point cloud and 2D image pose error of mobile mapping systems has always been a prominent topic, and a new panoramic image pose optimization method based on point cloud was proposed in this paper. First, 3D point cloud are projected to a depth panoramic image by image feature enhancement including masked discriminant projection, which could modify the image quality. Then a Siamese neural network with ResNet50 feature extractor is employed to extract projected image features. The results could be used to improve the rotation matrix errors between the panoramic image and the point cloud. The essence of the new proposed method is to reduce the relative error between the LiDAR and the camera, and to provide a good pose for the camera, which could modify the matching accuracy between the 3D point cloud and the 2D image. Experimental results show that the method studied in this paper can significantly improve the localization performance. The completion of this work helps to improve the accuracy and reliability of the mobile measurement scanning results data, which is important for point cloud coloring, object segmentation, map construction and navigation.

articleTitle: Automatic Night-Time Sea Fog Confidence Interval Detection Algorithm Based on Himawari-8 Data
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Sea fog is the primary factor affecting visibility at sea, severely limiting ship navigation. In order to solve the problems of high misjudgment rate of sea fog and poor stability of algorithm by traditional threshold method, this paper carries out a research on the Yellow Sea and Bohai Sea region based on Himawari-8 data, establishes histograms of brightness temperature difference of different bands, determines optimal confidence range of sea fog, and establishes automatic detection algorithm of night-time sea fog confidence intervals based on Himawari-8 data. In this paper, the algorithm is validated using the FY-4A data fog detection product, which has good stability, with a probability of detection (POD) of 84.6%, a false alarm ratio (FAR) of 11%, and a critical success index (CSI) of 90%. This study provides a reference for night-time sea fog forecasting and is of great significance for vessel navigation and fishery production activities.

articleTitle: A New Method for Planar Semantic Segmentation of Point Clouds in Indoor Scenes
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: The development of laser measurement technology has shifted the focus of 3D reconstruction from outdoor to indoor environments, leading to an increasing demand for creating precise indoor 3D semantic models. Semantic segmentation of indoor point cloud planes plays a crucial role in the process of indoor scene reconstruction. In this paper, we propose a method to build a plane model with vertical spatial coordinate axes to determine whether a point belongs to an inner group. We fit the indoor point cloud, remove a large number of clutter points, and perform an initial segmentation of the point cloud planes. We then utilize region growing algorithms and least squares method to extract parameters for ceiling, floor, and wall planes, and finally conduct semantic labeling. By comparing our method with existing approaches, we demonstrate that our approach effectively avoids the impact of indoor clutter while retaining the original point cloud features, leading to improved efficiency in plane segmentation and avoiding false positives.

articleTitle: Predictive Multimodal Wireless Localization Algorithm on a Two-Dimensional Plane based on MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Given the issue of positioning accuracy in high-rise buildings and urban areas within the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), the current approach primarily involves utilizing a combination of GNSS positioning methods to address these challenges. Consequently, the problem of mobile device positioning within cellular communication systems has become a widely researched focus. This paper reviews existing indoor positioning algorithms by establishing a base station network and designing a series of scenarios involving random mobile terminals. Various algorithms, such as TOA-LLOP, TOA-CHAN, TDOA-CHAN, TDOA-TAYLOR, RSSI-K-Nearest-Neighb or, RSSI-Weighted-K-Nearest-Neighbors, and RSSI-Nearest-Neighbors, were simulated, compared, and subjected to in-depth analysis. Through comparing these algorithms and their system performance, we delve into their advantages and limitations. Based on the screening results, we simulated a fusion algorithm, which significantly enhanced positioning accuracy by 29% under specific conditions.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Multi-Source-Free Domain Adaptation for High-Resolution Remote Sensing Scene Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: The existing studies on cross-domain classification of remote sensing scenes face challenges of low classification accuracy and strong dependence on source domain samples, particularly in complex urban scenes. In this paper, we proposed an unsupervised multi-source domain adaptation method for cross-domain classification of high-resolution remote sensing image scenes. Our method starts from extracting source domain featuresusing Swin Transformer as the backbone. We then used a cross-domain classification loss to train the target domain model. The loss consists of weighted information maximization and pseudo-labeling loss. The weighted information maximization loss is used to obtain the source domain feature distributions from the source domain model and combine multiple source domain models, while the pseudo-labeling loss is used to further align the feature distributions of the target and source domains. Our method can fully utilize the existing source domain samples to achieve effective classification of the target domain, while avoiding over-reliance on source domain data. We conducted multiple cross-domain classification experiments on four publicly available remote sensing scene classification datasets (AID, NWPU- RESISC45, U C Merced, and WHU-RS19) as well as the Fuzhou GF-2 dataset. The experimental results show that our proposed method achieves satisfactory cross-domain classification results for remote sensing scenes and remains applicable in complex urban scenes.

articleTitle: Retinex-Based Bilateral Filter and Discriminative Dictionary Learning for Enhancing Sonar Image
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Although the sonar image has been corrected, there exist in some problems with low illumination, and unclear edge texture. Therefore, it is urgent to solve scattered noise, image blur and uneven illumination in sonar image enhancement. This article takes side scan sonar images as the research object and decomposes them into low and high frequency sub band images by non-subsampled Shearlet transform (NSST). Retinex-based bilateral filter is applied to enhance the contrast of low frequency image. Image denoising of high frequency sub bands is achieved with sparse dictionary learning. Experimental results show that the enhanced image obtained by proposed method can clearly display the target texture, terrain change and edge information, and the speckle noise can be reduced and suppressed better. The objective indicator values are the best, reflecting the contrast, clarity, information content, and filtering performance of the image. The implementation of this work is conducive to providing clear target images and texture information for subsequent application research.

articleTitle: Extraction of Solar Photovoltaic Panels Based on High-Resolution Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Accurately and efficiently determining the installation positions, distribution, and total area of solar photovoltaic panels over a large area is important for investments and applications in photovoltaics. High-resolution optical satellite remote sensing imagery enables rapid and accurate extraction of ground-level objects. This provides the data foundation for automated extraction of photovoltaic panels based on deep learning. This paper utilizes high-resolution remote sensing imagery of solar photovoltaic panels. It employs the DeepLabv3+ semantic segmentation algorithm with the global convolutional network (GCN) to achieve a larger receptive field and enhance the network's global feature extraction capabilities. This improves the segmentation accuracy of photovoltaic panels. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved DeepLabv3+ model can achieve high-precision automated extraction of solar photovoltaic panels in complex remote sensing backgrounds.

articleTitle: Product Accuracy Analysis of Four Online Precise Point Positioning Service Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: The precise point positioning (PPP) of the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) can be considered as an alternative solution to differential GNSS positioning techniques. PPP technology has received wide attention due to its low cost and large user base. However, different online precise point positioning service systems apply different corrections, leading to variations in the processing of global satellite navigation system observations. To evaluate the performance of these systems, this study assesses four online precise point positioning service systems (APPS, CSRS-PPP, MagicGNSS, OPUS) in terms of their ability to process global satellite navigation system observation data. Using data from 18 International GNSS Service (IGS) stations distributed worldwide, the study analyzes the precision characteristics of three-dimensional coordinates, tropospheric delays, and clock corrections calculated by the four online PPP software systems. The analysis reveals that most of the stations achieve an accuracy of approximately 5mm in static positioning mode for APPS and CSRS-PPP. APPS performs slightly better in static positioning accuracy for high latitude regions compared to other dimensional regions of IGS stations. In dynamic positioning mode, the positioning deviations for the three online service systems are mostly around 5cm. OPUS results only provide static processed three-dimensional coordinates, which exhibit larger positioning deviations, reaching up to 4dm, indicating lower reliability. The clock correction accuracy of the three online PPP service systems does not show significant differences, with deviations around 10ns. In terms of tropospheric delay products, CSRS-PPP demonstrates the best interpolation accuracy. By conducting in-depth analysis of the global processing performance of these online PPP systems, we can better understand the performance strengths and limitations of different systems, thereby providing more reliable basis for precise GNSS positioning applications.

articleTitle: Research on ICESat-2 Single Photon Laser Point Cloud Denoising and Classification Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: The second-generation laser altimetry satellite ICESat-2, launched by the United States on September 15, 2018, uses micropulse photon counting lidar technology for the first time and performs elevation profiling type Earth observation. It is capable of realizing the global acquisition of geomorphological information with fast and efficient characteristics. Its advantages of micropulses, high frequency repetition, multiple beams and small footprint have made it a trend in the development of active earth observation laser altimetry in the future. Therefore, research on the processing and application methods of point cloud data collected by ICESat-2 is crucial. In this paper, the single photon laser point cloud data collected by ICESat-2 / ATLAS is taken as an example. Firstly, the OPTICS clustering algorithm is used to denoise the point cloud data, and then the least squares curve fitting method is used to classify the ground points and non-ground points by using the difference between the theoretical value and the actual value of the ground point elevation. Set a reasonable threshold to classify the ground points and non-ground points. The experiments in Shanghai and Qingdao prove the effectiveness of the two methods. The accuracy of denoising and classification can reach more than 95%, which can be applied to the processing of single-photon laser point cloud data.

articleTitle: IQSF Heading Correction Method Based on Indoor Geomagnetism
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: In mobile phone-based heading estimation, gyroscope cumulative drift is the main error source affecting pedestrian dead reckoning. In order to correct the estimated heading of the gyroscope with the help of the indoor effective magnetic field information, this paper is based on the idea of foot-tied IEZ+ framework, the pedestrian trajectory is preliminarily estimated by the gyroscope, IQSF was used to detect the stable magnetic field in the room to correct the pedestrian heading estimated by the gyroscope in this section. The interference section estimates the gyroscope heading angle with the heading information at the end of the stable section as the initial heading, thereby reducing the impact of drift and improving reliability. The comprehensive experimental results show that in the indoor test with a route length of 150m, the overall heading angle deviation of the proposed method is reduced by 0.5°~1.5° compared with the original method, and the deviation of the end of the route is reduced from 2.8m to 0.6m, and the heading and position accuracy are greatly improved.

articleTitle: Transformer-Based Feature Fusion Shrinkage Method for Remote Sensing Image Change Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: In the context of deep learning, remote sensing image change detection technology is advancing rapidly. At this stage, when compared to traditional convolutional neural networks, transformers exhibit a more robust capability for modeling global context. However, transformer also has limitations, on the one hand, it is easy to ignore local feature details, and on the other hand, it cannot sufficiently aggregate features in the decoding process. To solve these two problems, we propose a transformer-based feature fusion shrinkage network (FFSNet). First we introduce the coordinate attention module, which is capable of capturing precise positional information while handling inter-channel relationships, enhancing the capture of local details. In addition, we design a feature fusion compression decoder (FFSD), which is a pyramid-structured decoder that not only optimizes local details but also decodes them adequately. After extensive experiments, we demonstrate that our model performs significantly better than existing change detection models.

articleTitle: Research on Fine Modeling and Visualization of UAV Tilt Photogrammetry
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle tilt photogrammetry has the characteristics of high efficiency and low cost in large-scale 3D modeling applications, but this method is prone to problems such as voids and scratches when displaying individual models. This article analyzes the factors that affect the accuracy of 3D models, and uses multi-scale oblique photogrammetry methods to achieve precise modeling and visualization of individual buildings.

articleTitle: Improved Remote Sensing Classification and Detection Model Based on YOLOv7-Tiny
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that due to the complex background of optical remote sensing images, non-rotating frame target detection is easy to introduce background information, resulting in image classification that is prone to errors and missed detections, a classification model based on improved YOLOv7-tiny was proposed. On the one hand, this method introduces rotating frame detection to YOLOv7-tiny, which avoids the prediction frame containing background information and effectively improves the classification recognition rate of the model. On the other hand, it proposes a dual-scale loss function, which effectively solves the problem of the rotation angle of the square prediction frame. The problem cannot be optimized, and the high-precision coverage target of the rotation prediction frame is achieved. This method has been tested on remote sensing ship, aircraft, and car classification data sets. The experimental results show that the average detection accuracy of the improved network is increased by about 8 %.

articleTitle: Altimetry Accuracy Analysis of Sliding Spotlight Mode Interferometric SAR
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Multi-modal interference based on sliding spotlight mode, TOPS mode, etc. is an important development direction for InSAR systems in the next step. In the spaceborne sliding spotlight mode, the altimetry accuracy will be affected from multiple aspects due to the beam scanning in the azimuth direction. This article systematically analyzes the effects of azimuth ambiguity, azimuth scanning synchronization, registration, and resampling on the altimetry accuracy of sliding spotlight mode InSAR, which has certain reference value for the overall engineering design of InSAR systems.

articleTitle: A UNet-Like Hybrid Transformer for Efficient Semantic Segmentation of Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: In recent years, high-resolution remote sensing images have played a key role in areas such as precision agriculture, environmental protection, and economic evaluation. The rapid development of deep learning techniques has made Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Transformers the dominant approaches in semantic segmentation. However, the traditional Transformer architecture suffers from computational and memory burdens when processing large-scale high-resolution remote-sensing images. At the same time, the local nature of CNN convolutional layers limits the network to capture the global context. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid CNN- Transformer network based on the U-Net architecture, which achieves efficient semantic segmentation of remote sensing images by employing resnet18 in the backbone network and introducing the BiFormer attention module in the decoder. The experimental results show that the proposed network achieves 92.5 % F1 and 86.68% mIoU on the Potsdam dataset and 6.59G less in terms of model computational power (FLOPs) than the best existing method, UNetFormer, for the same input case. As a result, our approach is not only lightweight and efficient but also exhibits excellent performance in semantic segmentation.

articleTitle: Integrated Indoor and Outdoor Modeling Based on Multi-Source Laser Point Cloud Data
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: The traditional method of data collection and modeling using total stations is inefficient and challenging, especially when dealing with large buildings. Consequently, there is a growing trend towards adopting lidar scanners for data collection. This research paper focuses on obtaining point cloud data of a teaching building using three-dimensional laser scanning technology through various scanning methods: station scanner, airborne scanner, and handheld scanner. To process the acquired point cloud data, specialized software such as LiDAR360 and CloudCompare is utilized. These tools facilitate the fusion of multi-source point cloud data, involving point cloud cutting, denoising, coordinate registration, and overall point cloud integration. The end goal is to achieve a comprehensive representation of both indoor and outdoor point cloud data, providing a seamless display of the entire building. Additionally, the study utilizes SketchUp software to reconstruct an integrated three-dimensional scene of the teaching building, incorporating both indoor and outdoor elements. The results demonstrate that the integrated point cloud data successfully captures all the intricate details of the building, leading to an ideal three-dimensional model. Overall, the implementation of lidar scanners and advanced data processing techniques showcases the potential for highly accurate and detailed three-dimensional representations of complex structures like the teaching building studied in this research.

articleTitle: High-Precision Triangular Elevation Measurement Based on Correction of Refraction Coefficient of Unsteady Space Atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: In practical engineering, precise triangulation elevation measurements are required for the construction of large-span bridges across rivers. During this process, the atmospheric conditions above the water area exhibit complex and varying states in different times and spatial locations. The collection of environmental parameters such as temperature and pressure in the airspace above the water area is extremely difficult, making it impossible to establish a stable spatial atmospheric refraction coefficient model that satisfies high-precision triangulation elevation measurements. In this paper, based on the method of mathematical statistics, ignoring the atmospheric environment parameters, a non-uniform atmospheric refraction correction model is constructed according to the variation law of the atmospheric refraction coefficient in a certain time and space. Through combinatorial optimization and iterative calculation, the interference of atmospheric refraction coefficient in unstable space is solved to a certain extent. This method does not need to solve the problem of collecting atmospheric environmental parameters, and continuously adjusts the atmospheric refraction coefficient suitable for different time and space through program design. This method is effectively applied in a large-scale cross-river bridge under construction. At the same time, the algorithm design has strong practicability and flexibility, which greatly improves the accuracy of triangular elevation measurement in the unstable space of cross-river monitoring.

articleTitle: Modeling of Variation Characteristics of Visible LEO Satellite and Assessment of its Influence on Positioning
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites have some typical characteristics, such as fast movement speed, limited coverage area, high constellation density, and so on, which will inevitably lead to frequent changes in the number and geometric distribution of visible satellites for the ground receivers. Some studies about this have been done but only focus on the coverage analysis based on complex constellition simulation or empirical equivalent modeling. Wether it can be simply and accurately modeled or not and their impact on positioning are still need more in-depth exploration. Based on the spherical distribution characteristics of satellites, this paper first derived the estimation formulas for calculating the average coverage time of satellites and the change frequency of visible satellites. Meanwhile, a modified model for the variation characteristics of visible LEO satellites is proposed. Then, we analyzed the influence of the frequent change of visible satellites on the pseudorange and Doppler positioning accuracy. Finally, to evaluate the model, a typical simulation scenario was established for the average coverage time of satellites, the change frequency of visible satellites, and the influence on the positioning accuracy factor. Results show that, the error of the proposed model is 5.23%, and the error is reduced by 76.27% compared with traditional model, which can well approximate the satellite coverage time and the change frequency of visible satellites. It is also found that under the condition of the same number of satellites, the mean and variance of the Doppler Dilution of Precision (DDOP) are 64 and 480 times of the Geometric Dilution of Precision (GDOP), respectively.

articleTitle: Trajectory Optimization of Target Motion Based on Interactive Multiple Model and Covariance Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Indoor vehicle motion paths are often nonlinear and variable. The robust adaptive interactive multiple model covariance Kalman filter (IMM-RACKF) is proposed to track indoor maneuvering targets, to optimize the nonlinear and variable trajectory of the target motion. Firstly, by leveraging the advantage of interactive multiple model (IMM) for adaptability and the high precision and stability of the covariance Kalman filter (CKF), the CKF is incorporated into the IMM. Then, improve the fading factor in the robust adaptive Kalman filter (RAKF) using the innovation orthogonality principle, and incorporate it into CKF to enhance its robustness. Finally, the covariance matrix and the cross-covariance matrix of the abnormal measurement errors and model errors are used to suppress the influence on the filter. Simulation data analysis shows, when the measurement error is within the common range of 30 cm, the IMM-RACKF positioning error is only 14.7 cm. When the measurement error is 10cm and 30cm, and the model error is 50 cm, the trajectory estimation error of IMM-RACKF reaches only 9.4 cm and 34.5 cm, respectively. That is, the positioning accuracy and robustness of IMM-RACKF are far better than other filtering methods.

articleTitle: A Method for Extracting Laser Point Cloud Identification Lines with Boundary Feature Intersection Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: The proposed method in this study addresses the segmentation and extraction of arrow-type road markings in vehicle-mounted LiDAR point cloud data. The method begins by applying CSF ground filtering to the road point cloud to obtain ground points. Then, an OTSU threshold segmentation is performed on the ground point cloud to automatically search for the optimal threshold based on the desired number of objects and separate pixels into target and background categories for road marking segmentation. The segmented point cloud is then subjected to outlier removal using KD- Tree. Finally, mathematical morphological filtering is applied to denoise the marked point cloud. In case there is point cloud loss during the filtering process, a point cloud region growing algorithm is used to fill in the missing parts. The algorithm uses distance and reflectance intensity as growth criteria to determine if neighboring points of the seed point belong to the same feature condition, enabling the growth of the seed point and achieving complete marking effects. Afterward, Alpha shapes are utilized to extract the contours of the road markings, followed by multiple RANSAC iterations to segment the contours. For under-segmented or over-segmented line segments, different boundary features are used to establish specific adjustment models, allowing for the calculation of intersection coordinates as corner points of the road markings and eventually fitting regularized contour lines. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, particularly in handling special boundary cases.

articleTitle: Efficient Large Scale Reflectance Fusion Model for Generating High Temporal Landsat-like Data by Fusing Multi-Satellite Image
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: The emergence of spatiotemporal data fusion aims to address the inherent contradiction between temporal and spatial resolutions, seeking to generate high-resolution images in both dimensions. We present the Efficient Large-Scale Reflectance Fusion (ELSRF) approach on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform for resolving the temporal-spatial resolution trade-off in remote sensing data fusion. ELSRF effectively integrates Landsat and MODIS data, utilizing rubber-sheeting, Bayesian averaging, and weighted regression. Firstly, to bridge sensor disparities, rubber-sheeting and ordinary least squares methods are employed, yielding a fused MODIS-Landsat dataset. Then, Bayesian model averaging is harnessed to seamlessly integrate the initial fused data with climatological means, enhancing both precision and contextual understanding. Finally, ELSRF involves applying a weighted regression model, a critical step in refining the preliminary fusion outcomes. Validation demonstrates its accuracy in comparison with ground truth and existing methods: (1) Favorable accuracy is observed for both Landsat and Sentinel-2 comparisons; (2) ELSRF outperforms STARFM and FSDAF in visual and accuracy aspects; (3) NDVI indices derived from fusion data show reliable performance in validation with MOD13Q1 data. The experimental implementation of ELSRF on the GEE platform facilitates the swift and efficient operation of spatiotemporal fusion at a large scale.

articleTitle: Dense Remote Sensing Image Registration in Complex Terrain Areas Based on Feature Descriptors
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Due to differences in imaging methods, imaging conditions, and other factors between high-resolution optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) remote sensing images, these images exhibit distinct geometric characteristics and radiometric properties. Additionally, SAR images often suffer from severe speckle noise. As a result, achieving high-precision pixel-level registration (dense registration) between these images has remained a challenging problem. This paper presents a feature descriptor-based optical flow algorithm to address high-precision dense image registration. Unlike parameter-based registration methods that estimate transformation model parameters, the approach outlined in this paper aims to establish pixel correspondences between optical and SAR images. Firstly, dense descriptors based on structural similarity are created for both optical and SAR images to mitigate their intensity differences. The optical flow field is then estimated through optimizing an objective function, and a coarse-to-fine matching strategy is employed to handle large displacements while reducing computational costs. Experiments conducted with optical and SAR images in various scenarios have demonstrated the feasibility and effectiveness of this method. It exhibits strong robustness against noise and is capable of achieving high-precision registration between optical and SAR images even in the presence of local deformations in different scenes.

articleTitle: Conditional Adjustment with Parameters Based Solution of EIV Model
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: Errors-in-Variables (EIV) model is a mathematical model which takes into account the random errors of the design matrix, and it is widely used in the coordinate transformation, linear regression and polynomial fitting. The rigorous solution of EIV model generally requires the total Least-Squares (TLS) estimation, which is comparatively complicated in the calculating process and difficult to be applied in practice than Least-Squares (LS) estimation. In this contribution, the functional model of EIV is transformed into the form of conditional equation with parameters, which provides a novel perspective to understand EIV model. The transformed functional model treats the elements of the design matrix <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> as generalized or virtual observations, making the functional model easier to be understood and effortless to be solved. Then, the calculating formulas of the transformed mathematical model are derived by Lagrange Multiplier method combined with the conditions of the convergence point, named conditional adjustment with parameters based solution. Experimental results show that the proposed solution is the same as the existing TLS solution, which proves the feasibility and validity of the proposed solution. In summary, a novel perspective to understand EIV model is provided by transforming EIV model into the form of conditional equation with parameters in this contribution. Then, based on the transformed mathematical model, the calculating formulas equivalent to the classical TLS solution are strictly derived and fully examined.

articleTitle: Change Detection Based Land Cover Type Map Updated Method Using Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Geoscience and Remote Sensing Mapping (GRSM)
abstract: To obtain land cover change information related to forest and update the historical land cover map, a change detection and rule classification method is proposed. This paper takes Zalantun City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, as the study area and uses the Multivariate Alteration Detection method (MAD) to extract MAD differences; The MAD synthetic difference feature is calculated using each MAD difference feature to remove pseudo changes; The change detection result and the historical land cover type map are combined, and thus, the classification rules of the major land type change directions are analyzed and established. Then, the land cover information of the changed pixels in the later phase is obtained, thereby the land cover type map is updated. In the four years, the net growth area of forest land in Zalantun City was 42694hm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the growth rate was 2.54%. The major land cover change in Zalantun City was grassland-to-forest. Some small areas of mutual conversion between other land types were also detected. This paper develops a remote sensing method for updating land cover type maps based on change detection. The accuracy of change detection is 77.69% and the classification accuracy of land cover change types is 81.25%.
